title: The Day the Locks Stopped Working
story: Digital locks vanished. Imagine your house key suddenly fitting every door in the city.

title: Analogy: The Basement Safe
story: Imagine a thief who steals your locked safe. He can't open it now, but he's happy because he knows his grandson will have a magic drill to open it in 2030.
enterpriseInsight: The SNDL threat is real today.

interpretations.meaning: How much time you actually have left

title: Analogy: The Magic Mailbox
bullets: Easy to lock, hard to open
story: A blue postbox is like Public Key Encryption. Anyone can slide a letter in (Encrypt), but only the postman with the 'Secret Key' can open the back and read it.
enterpriseInsight: Infrastructure is built on this mailbox.

title: One Key (Symmetric)
story: The 'Netflix Password' problem. Sharing one key with everyone is great until you break up with someone.

title: Analogy: The Lazy Teenager
story: A Qubit is like a teenager in their room. Until you open the door (Measure), they are simultaneously 'Studying' and 'Gaming'. As soon as you walk in, they 'Collapse' into the 'Studying' state.

title: What is a Qubit?
story: A spinning coin is neither Heads nor Tails. It's a blur of both. That's a Qubit.

title: Analogy: The Maze Cheat Code
story: Classic computers are like a mouse in a maze trying every path. Shor's Algorithm is like a bird that flies above the maze and sees the exit immediately.
enterpriseInsight: Our mazes (RSA) are now visible from above.

interpretations.meaning: The repeating pattern of the maze

title: Analogy: The 500D Haystack
story: Classical security was a 3-digit combination lock. Lattice security is like hiding a specific grain of sand in a desert that has 500 different dimensions. Good luck finding it!
enterpriseInsight: Quantum computers still can't find that sand.

title: Banking: The SWIFT Collapse
story: A ghost in the machine transferring billions.

caseStudy.background: The SWIFT network handles trillions in daily cross-border transfers. It relies heavily on RSA/ECC for digital signatures.
caseStudy.technicalRisk: A quantum computer could forge these signatures in seconds.
caseStudy.mitigation: Implementation of Hash-based signatures and Lattice-based KEMs.
caseStudy.experimentSetup: Simulated banking environment with a 'Quantum Adversary'.
caseStudy.insight: Prevention of a global liquidity freeze.

title: The End (Or Beginning?)
story: Lights in your mind turning on. Like a new world appearing as the mist clears.

interpretations.meaning: Potential for a secure quantum future
